svg.aria-label: Diagram: Amazon Redshift's enable_large_strings_opt_in parameter turns on three capabilities and explicitly leaves a fourth thing unchanged. Set to Yes, strings stored in the SUPER data type can reach 16,000,000 bytes where the previous limit was 65,535 bytes, in-memory string functions can process VARCHAR values up to 16,000,000 bytes, and VARCHAR(MAX) resolves to VARCHAR(16000000) in expression contexts such as CAST expressions, views, user-defined functions and stored procedures. The non-change is that CREATE TABLE with VARCHAR(MAX) continues to create VARCHAR(65535) columns, so a table column never widens and SUPER becomes the only durable home for a large string. The figure is bounded in three directions at once: the string stops at 16,000,000 bytes, the individual SUPER object containing it can hold up to 16 MB of data so one maximal string leaves only about 4.6 percent of a 16 MiB object for everything else, and the table column stays at 65,535 bytes. On ingestion, loading into a SUPER column from a row-based format such as TEXT, CSV, JSON or AVRO requires the entire row to fit within the COPY scanner buffer which is 64 MB by default, while the columnar formats PARQUET and ORC are exempt from that scanner limit, and the TRUNCATECOLUMNS option applies only to VARCHAR columns so it does not trim an oversized string in a SUPER column. Operationally the opt-in has three edges: a provisioned cluster must be rebooted to apply the parameter, the real state is readable only with SELECT is_large_string_enabled() rather than from the parameter group, and once the parameter is set to Yes or No it cannot be reset to its default value of not set.
svg.title: Three capabilities, one parameter, and one explicit non-change
svg.text: Three capabilities behind one parameter — and one thing it deliberately leaves alone.
“Once you opt in through a database parameter …” — enable_large_strings_opt_in, default not set.
Set to Yes, three things change
strings in SUPER up to 16,000,000 bytes, where the limit was 65,535
in-memory functions VARCHAR values up to 16,000,000 bytes
VARCHAR(MAX) in views resolves to VARCHAR(16000000) in CAST, views, UDFs, procedures
“CREATE TABLE with VARCHAR(MAX) continues to create VARCHAR(65535) columns.”
The column never widens. SUPER becomes the only durable home for a string above 65,535 bytes.
Bounded in three directions at once
the string 16,000,000 bytes
the object 16 MB — one maximal string leaves ~4.6% of it for everything else
the column 65,535 bytes — unchanged
Getting it in
Row-based (TEXT, CSV, JSON, AVRO): the whole
row must fit the 64 MB COPY scanner buffer.
PARQUET and ORC are exempt from it.
TRUNCATECOLUMNS does not trim SUPER.
The opt-in has edges
Provisioned cluster: reboot to apply.
Verify with is_large_string_enabled(),
not from the parameter group.
Once set to Yes or No, it cannot be reset.
Measure your string sizes before enabling it: the gap from 65,535 to 16,000,000 bytes is wide.
Most payloads near the old ceiling are nowhere near the new one, and a payload near the new one is already
against the 16 MB object limit, which no parameter moves.
The default is a third state — not set — and it does not come back.
